name: Question 15
problem:
Find ${lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)$ for the function given by

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & \text{ for }\,x<-1 \\ 3 & \text{ for }\,x>1.\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
Approaching $x=-1$ from the left, we have $x<-1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={x}^{2}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}{x}^{2} \\  & =(-1)^{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, approaching $x=1$ from the right, we have $x>1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}3=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15

Find limx→(−1)−f(x) and limx→1+f(x) for the function given by f(x)={x2 for x<−13 for x>1.

a
limx→(−1)−f(x)=−1,limx→1+f(x)=3
b
limx→(−1)−f(x)=1,limx→1+f(x)=3
c
limx→(−1)−f(x)=DNE,limx→1+f(x)=DNE
d
limx→(−1)−f(x)=DNE,limx→1+f(x)=3
e
limx→(−1)−f(x)=1,limx→1+f(x)=DNE
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Approaching x=−1 from the left, we have x<−1, so we use the expression f(x)=x2. We get limx→(−1)−f(x)=limx→(−1)−x2=(−1)2=1.

On the other hand, approaching x=1 from the right, we have x>1, so we use the expression f(x)=3. We get limx→1+f(x)=limx→1+3=3.
